vit3.architecture: the repo's DINO-WM ViTPredictor class (src/models/dinowm/vit.py) with the checkpoint's settings: width 404, depth 6, 16 heads, head size 64, MLP 2048; num_patches 196; num_frames 3 (DINO-WM's history window, causal attention across frames)
vit3.tokens: the 28x28x8 channel-PCA latent grouped into 2x2 patches -> 196 tokens of 32 numbers, linearly embedded to 384, concatenated with a 20-number action embedding (DINO-WM concatenates action and proprio embeddings to reach 404); output head maps each token back to its 2x2x8 residual
vit3.recipe: identical to cell E: deterministic step model, 50/50 G or rendered perturbed starts, 19-step unrolled loss with input noise 0.1 x residual std, hold-10/30 weight 2, AdamW 3e-4 cosine, batch 32, 30,000 steps, seed 0, Phase-1 enriched data, last step kept
vit3.evaluation: Phase-1 held-out set H (160 states, 75 forks) with the Phase-1 evaluation (G starts from perception draw j, execution snippet j; unchanged split test); forks caught, false alarms, side agreement, spread diagnostics, under-training rule (Phase-1 addendum 1)
vit3.comparison: cell E (same recipe, conv step model): 69% / 8%
vit3.history: a window of the last 3 latents. At the start the two missing past frames are copies of the start latent (blocks are at rest at a chunk start); during the 19-step rollout the window is filled with the model's own predictions, as DINO-WM rolls out. Training uses the same window inside the unrolled loss.

conv3.architecture: cell E's convolutional step model (step3_world_model.Transition body: width 128, 6 FiLM residual blocks) with the same 3-latent history window concatenated along channels
conv3.recipe: identical to vit3 (and to cell E apart from the history window)
conv3.purpose: separates the effect of history from the effect of the transformer

comparison: E (conv, 1 frame): 69% / 8%; vit3 vs conv3 isolates the architecture; conv3 vs E isolates history
selection_rule: rank E, vit3, conv3 by (forks caught - false alarms) on H, as Phase 1
